chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed God the Honorable, the Exalted has said: 'I have honored My servants with three things: I cast upon them the stench after the soul leaves, and had it not been for that, a beloved one would not bury the deceased. I cast upon them relief after the calamity, and had it not been for that, none of them would enjoy their life. I created this creature (worms/bugs) and gave it dominion over wheat and barley, and had it not been for that, their kings would hoard them as they hoard gold and silver.'

key_terms.الدَّابَّة: The creature (referring to worms/bugs that eat grain)
key_terms.الرِّيح: Stench or foul odor (specifically of the corpse)

ai.seo_question: What are the three blessings God granted to His servants according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlighting three specific divine mercies (*ni'am*) that maintain cosmic balance and social stability. The narration emphasizes the wisdom behind the stench of the dead (*hamim*) prompting burial, the psychological solace (*salwah*) following grief, and the role of pests in preventing the hoarding of grain by rulers, thereby ensuring economic accessibility for the common people.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-87 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Muhammad ibn Abdul Jab’bar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma’il, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“Indeed God the Honorable the exalted has said, ‘I have honored my servants by granting them three blessings. First, I have made their corpse stink after their soul leaves their body. Had it not been so, no one’s relatives would ever bury their deceased loved ones. I have granted them a relief after mourning. Had it not been so, no one could enjoy life. I have created bugs and gave them dominion over wheat and barely. Had it not been so, the Kings and the rulers would have stored them in their houses just as they store gold and silver.”
